item.title: Satellite Images Reveal Aftermath Of Drone Attack On Saudi Arabia’s Biggest Refinery
item.description: New GEOINT from spatial intelligence firm Vantor shows high-resolution satellite imagery of the aftermath of a reported Iranian drone strike early Monday on Saudi Aramco’s Ras Tanura complex. This attack has taken Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery offline. Vantor’s satellite imagery shows visible damage across multiple refinery structures, though the full extent of the disruption and physical destruction remains unclear. item.description: In borderless Britain, it seems as if barely a day goes by without some monstrosity being committed by a migrant who should never have been in the country in the first place. item.title: Gulf States Say They’ve Shot Down More Than 1,500 Iranian Missiles, Drones
item.description: Five Gulf nations that host U.S. military installations claim they have collectively shot down more than 1,500 Iranian missiles and drones since the United States and Israel launched their joint attack at 9:45 a.m. Tehran time on Feb. 28. item.title: Dubai Contains Fire From Drone-Related Incident Near US Consulate
item.description: Dubai authorities on Wednesday, March 4, confirmed that a fire resulting from a drone-related incident has been “fully extinguished”. The incident took place near the US Consulate in the city. Authorities added that emergency teams responded immediately and that no injuries have been reported. item.title: UAE Airlines Continue Limited Operations as Regular Flights Remain Disrupted
item.description: The General Civil Aviation Authority has announced the gradual resumption of limited flights across airports in the UAE, as authorities move to assist thousands of travellers stranded by recent regional developments. Under the revised operational plan, air traffic is currently being managed at a rate of 48 flights per hour through designated emergency corridors.
